item.title: Jakarta Government Reveals Massive Economic Impact Of Ye’s Concert
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ye's Jakarta concert brought an estimated $25 million in economic activity to the city, Governor Pramono Anung said.
item.content:encoded:
Ye‘s Jakarta concert generated an estimated $25 million in economic activity, according to Governor Pramono Anung.

The governor shared that estimate Monday, October 26, following the rapper’s Saturday performance at Gelora B### Karno Main Stadium.

The official report also put ticket sales at about $18 million, while Pramono said hotels, shops, transport and tourism benefited.

That account offered no detailed breakdown of how officials arrived at the broader estimate of the concert’s economic impact.

Before the show, promoter Raw Vision Collective said 20,500 people outside Indonesia had bought tickets, according to Indonesia Expat.

Karen Tjahja, who led marketing and communications for the promoter, gave that sales update at an October 22 press conference. Among buyers abroad, Australia ranked first, with Singapore and Malaysia following it in the promoter’s count of international ticket sales.

Those figures captured purchases ahead of the concert, leaving them separate from a final tally of fans inside the stadium.

Tjahja said other events that week had made flights harder to find, prompting the promoter to arrange extra charter services.

Tjahja said the overseas sales could mark a new high for international visitors at an Indonesian solo concert.

The concert had offered fans a hotel option from the start, with packages advertised when tickets went on sale in July.

AllHipHop’s earlier coverage described the October 24 booking as the only Southeast Asian date on Ye’s 2026 tour schedule.

Organizers then expected as many as 77,000 people, a pre-show projection that didn’t indicate how many ultimately attended Saturday.

The stop also returned him to a region where he had played Singapore Indoor Stadium in 2008 and SingFest in 2010.

The tour also featured The Globe Stage, a 360-degree production designed to put fans around the performance and inside the experience.

MRT Jakarta’s Mega Tarigan, its director of operations and maintenance, announced the transit changes Friday, October 23.

MRT Jakarta also announced longer train hours for fans and the public, extending service until 1:30 a.m. Sunday, October 25.

item.title: 50 Cent Sues Rick Ross’ Ex Tia Kemp For $6M Over Posts About Sire Jackson
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 50 Cent sought at least $6 million from Tia Kemp in a federal lawsuit over social media posts about his teenage son Sire.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent sought at least $6 million from Tia Kemp in a new federal lawsuit over posts about his son, Sire, according to Billboard.

The outlet obtained the complaint, filed in Los Angeles on October 26. Curtis Jackson sued Tiallondra “Tia” Kemp on behalf of 14-year-old Sire, identified as S.J., alleging defamation, invasion of privacy and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

His lawyers accused Kemp of inventing a medical diagnosis and sexually degrading claims involving Sire’s mother, Daphne Joy. They alleged she kept posting after a cease-and-desist letter.

“But autism is not shameful,” the lawyers wrote in the filing quoted by Billboard.

The federal case followed a separate Florida petition seeking an injunction against Kemp over alleged cyberstalking, first reported by TMZ.

The dispute had already drawn a public response from Sire’s father. As AllHipHop previously reported, he shared news of the restraining-order request on Instagram and objected to using claims about a child’s health as an insult.

“This is the greatest example of bullying a minor saying he is on the spectrum,” 50 wrote.

He also said he had friends whose children were on the spectrum and said the subject was no joke.

Kemp shares a son, William Roberts III, with Rick Ross. Her comments about Sire followed 50’s public taunts about an alleged attack on William.

The rapper mocked William for calling police and used the incident to revisit Ross’ past work as a correctional officer. He also offered help with bond and a lawyer for the accused attacker; it was unconfirmed whether he paid anything.

The relationship between 50 and Kemp had looked different in June 2025. He offered her a talk show while sharing a clip of her on Instagram. His pitch suggested she could replace Wendy Williams, bringing Kemp into another public exchange tied to his long feud with Ross.

In the clip, Kemp complained that people kept comparing her to cats. The rapper paired the video with an invitation to make a deal. The offer put her outspoken social media persona at the center of his television pitch.

The new court lawsuit mirrors an earlier Ross feud that left 50 facing a multimillion-dollar obligation to another woman.

Lastonia Leviston, who shares a daughter with Ross, won a privacy case over a sex video featuring her and a former boyfriend.

The video circulated in 2009, with 50 appearing as the character Pimpin’ Curly and making remarks about Leviston while taunting Ross.

Ross did not appear in the footage, which became part of the rappers’ feud years before the current dispute with Kemp.

Jurors initially awarded Leviston $5 million, and 50 filed for bankruptcy on July 13, 2015, before they added $2 million in punitive damages.

That brought the verdict to $7 million, but the later bankruptcy agreement set Leviston’s claim at $6 million.

Judge Ann Nevins asked whether he understood that he would still owe Leviston even if he sought bankruptcy protection again.

“That’s not gonna happen,” 50 told the judge during the July 2016 hearing, according to The Associated Press.

Kemp did not immediately answer Billboard’s request for comment. On TikTok, she told him he could not bully her.

item.title: America Prepares Military Bases For Catastrophe As Other Nations Warn Citizens To Prepare
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.category: signs the world is coming to an end
item.description: As the Pentagon prepares military bases to survive 90 days of catastrophe, European governments are urging citizens to prepare, raising urgent questions about America's public readiness.
item.content:encoded:
America is preparing its military to survive a potential national catastrophe for 90 days, but a troubling question remains: Is anybody making sure ordinary Americans are equally prepared?

The Pentagon has launched a sweeping initiative called FORTRESS, which stands for Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply, and Survivability. Announced September 30 by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the program aims to make American military installations less dependent on civilian infrastructure.

READ ALSO: Military Discipline Crumbles After Hegseth Protects Kid Rock…

According to an October 25 Fox News report, military bases are being prepared to operate independently for at least 90 days if war, cyberattacks or infrastructure failures disrupt electricity, fuel supplies and transportation networks. The plan includes nuclear microreactors, independent power systems and strategic reserves.

That sounds like serious business. And it is.

Meanwhile, governments across Europe are delivering increasingly explicit preparedness messages to their citizens.

Sweden distributed updated emergency preparedness literature in 2024 under the unmistakable title “In Case of Crisis or War.” The publication addresses military attacks, evacuations, communication failures and household survival.

On October 22, Britain launched “Be Ready,” a three-year campaign encouraging residents to stockpile enough essential supplies for 72 hours. The government’s recommendations include drinking water, food, emergency equipment and plans for service interruptions.

The European Union has also embraced a broader preparedness strategy, recommending that households become self-sufficient for at least three days.

So, what about America?

The United States has FEMA and Ready.gov, which provide emergency preparedness instructions. Americans are encouraged to maintain supplies, establish communication plans and prepare for disasters. However, there is no mention of war, attacks or the Pentagon’s military initiatives. This is where the conversation becomes uncomfortable.

If military planners are preparing for prolonged disruption, shouldn’t everyday citizens receive equally prominent guidance about the risks?

Consider families living paycheck to paycheck, elderly residents dependent on electricity-powered medical equipment and communities already struggling with unreliable infrastructure. Preparing for even three days without essential services can be a financial challenge.

To be clear, FORTRESS does not establish that war or nationwide collapse is imminent. Military preparedness is not evidence of a secret evacuation plan or an impending attack.

Nevertheless, Americans deserve transparent communication about potential threats and practical instructions for protecting their families.

Because national security should involve protecting the people, not merely keeping military installations operational.

And if the government is preparing for the worst, perhaps it is time to make sure the rest of us understand what that preparation means.

I want to know.

item.title: Donald Trump Offers $1M Voter Fraud Reward
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Donald Trump offered a $1 million voter fraud reward, but the White House provided no details on where the money would come from.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump offered $1 million for voter fraud tips on October 26, eight days before the midterm election, while leaving the source of the money unanswered.

His Truth Social post covered both past elections and the coming 2026 vote. The promised payment depended on an arrest and a conviction.

Tipsters would be paid “upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!” he wrote.

The White House provided no further details about the offer, according to ABC News. The outlet reported that it was unclear where the reward money would come from. The post itself did not name an agency that would run the program or explain how someone should submit a claim.

It followed another cash promise. Last week, Trump announced a separate whistleblower program offering people who successfully exposed fraud a share of money recovered by the government. ABC reported that the proposed cut was 1% and that Trump said he would decide whether someone received an award.

The president also pushed the SAVE America Act, which would require voter identification at the polls and proof of citizenship to register. The House passed that measure, but it failed repeatedly in the Senate, ABC reported.

The fight over access to the ballot predates this reward. In AllHipHop’s March 2025 coverage, voting rights groups warned that Trump’s citizenship-document executive order could shut out eligible voters.

Their concern included people in marginalized communities who lacked easy access to the required papers. Critics also challenged the order’s threat to withhold federal election money from states that refused to comply.

Ahead of this year’s election, the FBI issued its own warning about election crimes on October 15. Its examples included voting twice, tampering with ballots and threatening voters with physical or financial harm.

The bureau also warned against deliberately giving qualified voters false information about when, where or how to vote to keep them from casting ballots.

Existing reporting channels are available. Federal guidance at USAGov directs suspected voter fraud complaints to election officials, local FBI offices or federal prosecutors. People who face voter intimidation or suppression can contact election officials or the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division.

For voters making plans for November 3, the Federal Election Commission identifies state and local election offices as the place to check registration questions, polling locations and voting hours.

item.title: Jimmy Kimmel Grosses Himself Out Copying “Horny” Donald Trump Lusting Over Nicki Minaj
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jimmy Kimmel copied Donald Trump's gestures after his comments about Nicki Minaj's backside and said he was grossing himself out.
item.content:encoded:
Jimmy Kimmel tried out Donald Trump’s moves after the president’s comments about Nicki Minaj’s backside, then admitted the impression was making him uncomfortable.

During his October 26 monologue on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” the host copied Trump’s lip licking, air punch and pursed mouth as his studio audience laughed. The gestures followed Trump’s remarks about Minaj at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan.

“Honestly, I’m grossing myself out even doing it. Horny Donald is my least favorite Donald of all of them.”

Kimmel also questioned how Fox News would have reacted if Joe Biden had made the same comments about the rapper. His routine turned the president’s words and physical reaction into material for Monday’s show.

The Port Huron exchange happened Sunday, October 25. Trump called Minaj’s backside “one hell of a beautiful ass” and added, “That’s hard to miss.”

He brought up Minaj while explaining why he had looked over Ohio Sen. Jon Husted. Trump tied that earlier moment to learning about Husted’s college football career and his reputation for hard tackles.

His remarks about Husted at an October 12 rally in Youngstown had drawn coverage before the Michigan stop.

Nicki Minaj had traveled to Michigan aboard Air Force One. During the flight, she told White House communications director Steven Cheung that she supported Trump.

She praised his approach to negotiations and said his experience recovering from financial trouble helped explain her confidence in how he handles the country’s finances.

Cheung shared the interview on X and joked that they might have found a new White House press secretary.

item.title: Papoose Brags About Knocking Out Eazy The Block Captain, But Illseed Remembers Something
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Papoose is celebrating his alleged knockout of Eazy The Block Captain in a new freestyle, but AllHipHop remembers when he wanted the original report taken down.
item.content:encoded:
Papoose is bragging about allegedly knocking out Eazy The Block Captain again, but I remember a time when he apparently wanted that very story to disappear.

And I have a little something to add to the historical record.

Back when reports first surfaced about Papoose allegedly putting hands on Eazy, AllHipHop was among the outlets reporting the situation practically in real time. What most people don’t know is that Papoose actually reached out to our platform.

Yep. He contacted us.

From what I recall, he wasn’t particularly enthusiastic about having that information circulating publicly. I did not talk to him, bt we had an internal hddleMy impression was that he wanted to minimize the exposure surrounding the alleged incident. Maybe he was concerned about potential legal consequences. I cannot say that for certain.

What I can say is that he wanted the report taken down, and I believe we accommodated his request. Frankly, that was an unusual amount of cooperation on our part.

We never heard back from him. Life continued, and the alleged altercation eventually became another infamous chapter in Hip-Hop relationship history.

Fast forward to October 2026.

Papoose has released a car freestyle called “Food For Thought,” responding to Eazy’s recent lyrical attacks on him and Claressa Shields. And apparently, whatever reluctance he once had about discussing the confrontation has evaporated.

“I caught a speeding ticket I gave him so many speed knots,” Papoose raps.

Now, that’s quite an interesting position considering the history.

Of course, Eazy has repeatedly denied being knocked unconscious, although he acknowledged getting punched. An alleged eyewitness previously supported that distinction.

So, who are we supposed to believe?

Meanwhile, Remy Ma appears conspicuously absent from this latest exchange. Papoose even references her lack of response in the freestyle.

Could she be completely finished with Eazy and all this foolishness? I don’t know. Her silence certainly doesn’t establish that, but I wonder if she’s simply moved on mentally.

By the way, Remy is looking fantastic these days.

Anyway, here’s where I land.

These are grown adults with children, careers and considerable influence. Papoose has a daughter watching his example. And with an election approaching, I’m increasingly interested in what we’re doing to secure our collective future.

Maybe it’s time to retire this particular fight.

There are bigger battles ahead, and not all of them require fists.

What do you think?

item.title: Nipsey Hussle’s Marathon Burger Lands At LAX With Exclusive Breakfast Menu
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Marathon Burger opened at LAX Terminal 1, adding an exclusive breakfast menu as Blacc Sam expanded Nipsey Hussle's family brand.
item.content:encoded:
Nipsey Hussle‘s Marathon Burger has opened at Los Angeles International Airport, bringing the family business to the terminal the rapper and his brother once used.

Samiel “Blacc Sam” Asghedom, Hussle’s brother and co-owner of the chain, announced the Terminal 1 location on Instagram. The terminal held a personal connection for the brothers, who often passed through it when flying out of Los Angeles.

Travelers will be able to order most of the chain’s usual menu, Asghedom said. The airport restaurant also has an exclusive breakfast menu, giving the new location something beyond the food served at its other shops.

The move followed work on Terminal 1’s food court.

In an October 12 construction update, Los Angeles World Airports said it was rebranding Betcha Burger as Marathon while nearby Ace Tacos was becoming Kogi BBQ. Both projects were scheduled to finish in mid-October.

The airport’s current Terminal 1 map now lists Marathon Burger in the departures-level food court alongside Kogi BBQ, Einstein Bros. Bagels, Chick-fil-A and Panda Express. The terminal map covers Gates 9 through 18.

For Blacc Sam, the airport shop extends a restaurant business built around a plan he shared with Hussle. Before the original restaurant launched, he told FOX 11 that the brothers had worked together cooking and talked about running their own restaurant.

The first Marathon Burger opened in Los Angeles in March 2025.

A Venice Beach location followed that June. During that expansion, Asghedom told FOX 11 that creating jobs was among the parts of the business that made the team most proud.

The chain later reached Long Beach, where Snoop Dogg and his son Cordell became investors. Blacc Sam credited the pair with introducing the team to the mayor and helping bring the restaurant downtown.

That location opened on March 1, 2026.

The LAX restaurant joins a Southern California footprint that also includes Canoga Park.

Blacc Sam has also discussed taking the business beyond the region. In August, he announced plans for a Las Vegas location with a drive-thru and 24-hour service.

item.title: Tia Kemp Tells 50 Cent “You Can’t Bully Me” After Legal Filing
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: 50 Cent is taking Rick Ross' ex Tia Kemp to court over alleged online harassment of his teenage son, turning a bitter feud into a legal showdown.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent has officially taken his feud with Tia Kemp into a Florida courtroom, and this time, the notoriously ruthless Hip-Hop troll is fighting to protect his 14-year-old son.

Now, we all know 50 Cent is one of the most relentless antagonists in the history of Hip-Hop. This man has practically turned trolling into a profitable subsidiary of his entertainment empire. But apparently, there are some things even he considers off limits.

And his son Sire Jackson is one of them.

Curtis Jackson filed a petition Monday (October 26) in Miami-Dade County seeking legal protection for Sire against Tia Kemp, who shares a son with Rick Ross. Wow.

The accusations are ugly.

50 alleges Kemp targeted his son in four separate online publications over six days. Among the allegations are derogatory comments about the teenager’s speech and development, including unsubstantiated speculation about autism.

The petition also accuses Kemp of publishing an image of Sire alongside sexually explicit material involving an adult woman.

That is quite a disturbing allegation regardless of what the beef is with 50.

Apparently, his attorneys attempted to resolve the situation without involving a judge. They reportedly sent Kemp a cease and desist letter demanding that she remove the offensive material and stop targeting his child.

Her alleged response?

“F u and ya lawyers.”

Well, that certainly wasn’t the response the legal team was hoping for.

Tia was like:

Kemp has since responded to the legal action, accusing 50 of provoking the conflict in the first place. I mean…he sort of picked the right and wrong one at the same time.

“You can’t bully me, b***h.”

We need a reminder on how thing all kicked off for the new era. The dispute intensified after 50 mocked reports that Rick Ross and Kemp’s adult son had been assaulted. And then allegedly freed the man that allegedly attacked him. That’s a lot of allegedlies. LOL! Kemp subsequently directed her anger toward 50’s family. Seems fair, right?

Can somebody who has built an enormous reputation tormenting his adversaries successfully convince a judge that another person’s online conduct has crossed into harassment?

Legally, his own reputation for trolling doesn’t automatically undermine his petition. His kid is a kid. Her kid is in college. The question is whether Kemp’s alleged conduct meets Florida’s requirements for an injunction.

50 wants immediate temporary protection, followed by a final injunction after a hearing. There is no confirmed ruling granting that request.

For all the entertainment these celebrity feuds provide, children shouldn’t become collateral damage in battles between adults. Or kids in my opinion. That big boy getting pistol whipped is not something to celebrate.

We’ll see what the judge says.

item.title: Jon Stewart Mocks Donald Trump’s Fixation On Nicki Minaj’s Backside
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jon Stewart mocked Donald Trump's focus on Nicki Minaj's body after the rapper joined the president at his Michigan rally.
item.content:encoded:
Jon Stewart turned Donald Trump’s attention to Nicki Minaj’s backside into material for Monday’s “The Daily Show,” taking aim at the president a day after the rapper joined his Michigan campaign stop.

The host set up the segment around the midterm elections and voters’ concerns about prices, the economy and Iran before showing Trump’s remarks.

“How the fuck is this real?” Stewart asked. He also joked about Trump’s expression as Minaj spoke.

“He’s like Yogi Bear floating towards a pie on a windowsill.”

The comments followed Trump’s Sunday rally in Port Huron, at McMorran Place Arena as Republicans sought votes ahead of the November 3 elections.

Trump brought up Minaj’s body while discussing his remarks about Ohio Sen. Jon Husted. He called her backside “one hell of a beautiful ass” and added, “That’s hard to miss.”

He later said he hoped Minaj hadn’t been insulted and spoke about his affection for her. Nicki Minaj had flown to Michigan with Trump aboard Air Force One.

In an interview with White House communications director Steven Cheung, she explained why she trusted him to handle the economy. She cited his recovery from financial problems as part of her faith in his judgment.

Work habits were another part of her pitch.

“He outworks people who are half his age,” she said. Minaj also praised how he dealt with other countries, tying her support to his approach to business and negotiations.

Onstage, the rapper pledged to keep backing Trump and told him, “If you run again, I will support you again.”

Her immediate appeal focused on two Michigan Republicans: Senate candidate Mike Rogers and gubernatorial candidate John James. She urged the crowd to vote for both men and led chants of their names.

The trip added to a run of public appearances that linked Minaj to the administration.

In September, she appeared with Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler during an interview with Laura Ingraham.

Nicki Minaj also served as a judge for the Million Dollar Pitch Competition alongside entrepreneurs Grant Cardone and Joe Gebbia. The contest offered a $1 million prize to a business.

item.title: Alicia Keys & Swizz Beatz Turn To Lowrider Soul For “Lovers Rose”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz revealed a seven-track Lovers Rose project rooted in soul and lowrider culture, expected in early 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz took their next joint project into lowrider territory, revealing a seven-track album called Lovers Rose that pulls from Chicano soul and Latin musical traditions.

The couple discussed the record in Vogue Italia’s November cover story. Keys’ team announced an expected arrival in early 2027 and described the project as a sonic installation.

Keys described a warm, calm sound outside their usual New York style, while Swizz discussed writing together and sharing ideas in the room.

“Working with my wife, of whom I am still a huge fan, is amazing. Being able to be in the same room with her, writing together, sharing ideas, and giving the audience something they don’t expect from the two of us is incredible,” Swizz Beatz said.

The pair had worked on music together long before Lovers Rose. In December 2010, Swizz’s Monster Mondays series released Keys’ “Speechless”, which featured Eve and centered on their newborn son Egypt. Keys presented it as a holiday gift for fans. The track sampled Kanye West’s “Devil In A New Dress.”

“It’s not the typical ‘New York sound.’ There’s a sense of peace, of warmth, a vibration that allows you to relax and disconnect from the chaos of a world that scares us,” adds Keys. “‘ Lovers Rose’ is an invitation to let your nervous system breathe,” Alicia Keys revealed.

The car connection has already extended beyond the studio.

Earlier this month, BRABUS introduced a Lovers Rose clothing collection made with the couple. The range included T-shirts, hoodies, track pants, shorts and caps, with rose imagery worked into the designs.

BRABUS drew inspiration from Keys and Swizz’s own BODO Coupe. The car was named for company founder Bodo Buschmann. The brand framed the clothes around the couple’s interests in music, design and cars, giving the Lovers Rose name a home in fashion before the record arrives.

Their creative partnership has also brought Black visual art into museums. The Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego’s presentation of “Giants” drew on their personal Dean Collection, with more than 130 works and 37 Black American and diasporic artists.

The Brooklyn Museum organized the exhibition in 2024; it included paintings, photographs, sculptures and installations. Its artists included Gordon Parks, Jean-Michel Basquiat, Amy Sherald, Kehinde Wiley and Mickalene Thomas. San Diego marked its first West Coast showing. Swizz also curated an official playlist for that run.

The two extended that work into film this year, joining the executive producers of “Black Is Beautiful: The Kwame Brathwaite Story”. Directed by Yemi Bamiro, the documentary examines the photographer and activist whose images helped shape the Black Is Beautiful movement.
